documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u after nephrology. AA amyloidosis on fat pad biopsy (letter 12/6 reviewed): from long-standing RA; nephrotic-range proteinuria, normal echo, no monoclonal protein. Nephrology started losartan 25 - adding to our list. Saw rheumatology in January; they are working on the new medication with her insurance, not started yet as far as she knows.
Swelling a bit less with low-salt eating. Still tired. Sugars unchanged.
Exam: BP per flowsheet. Lungs clear. 2+ edema to mid-shin. Abd soft.
A/P:
1. AA amyloidosis with nephrotic syndrome - per nephrology/rheum. Losartan 25 daily. BMP today.
2. HTN - on amlodipine, HCTZ, losartan.
3. T2DM - A1c today. Metformin ok at current kidney function; will watch.
4. Requested rheumatology note.
RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM/HTN/renal f/u.
Rheumatology started tocilizumab 162 mg SC weekly in January for the amyloidosis; she injects on Sundays. No letter from them yet - adding from her report and the specialty pharmacy label she brought. Still on MTX 15 weekly, folic acid, prednisone 5.
Feels somewhat less wiped out. Legs still swell by evening. No infections. No dizziness. Smoking ~10/day.
Exam: Lungs clear. Heart regular. Edema to mid-shin bilaterally, 1-2+. Abd soft.
Labs back this afternoon: albumin 3.1, UACR 2600 - still heavy protein loss. A1c and CBC still pending.
A/P:
1. AA amyloidosis/nephrotic - on tocilizumab (rheum) + losartan (nephro). Copy labs to both.
2. T2DM - A1c pending.
3. HTN.
4. Immunosuppression x3 - reviewed infection warning signs; call with fever.
RTC 3-4 months; front desk to book.

documents.body: Janet - the rest of Friday's labs: A1c still in the mid 8s, kidney function about the same as winter, blood count steady with a normal neutrophil count on the new injection. Copies went to nephrology and rheumatology. Please book your late-summer visit.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
OUTSIDE EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN NOTE
Visit 05/29/2025

61F with RA (methotrexate, prednisone, tocilizumab per patient), type 2 diabetes, recently diagnosed AA amyloidosis. For about two weeks, sudden bouts of severe spinning whenever she rolls onto her right side in bed or tips her head back to reach a high cupboard. Each lasts under a minute and leaves her nauseated. No hearing change, no ringing, no weakness, numbness, speech or vision trouble. NKDA.

BP 130/85. Cardiovascular exam normal. Neurologic exam nonfocal: cranial nerves intact, normal finger-nose, normal gait.
Dix-Hallpike to the right: brief burst of nystagmus with vertigo lasting less than a minute, fading on its own.

Impression: benign paroxysmal positional vertigo, right.
Treatment: canalith repositioning (Epley) performed in the department; symptoms improved on re-testing.
Disposition: home. Home Epley instructions given. Follow up with PCP; return for new neurologic symptoms.

documents.title: Patient Portal Message
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Patient: Wanted you to know I went to the ER on 5/29 for the room spinning. They did a head maneuver and it's been gone since. I did the exercises at home a few days. All good now.

documents.title: Patient Portal Message
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Thanks for letting us know - we received the ER record last week. That's the classic inner-ear crystal vertigo; if it returns, the same home maneuver usually works, and call if it doesn't settle or you notice anything different (weakness, speech, vision).

documents.body: Patient: I lost the sight in my right eye Wednesday after I banged my head on the door frame in the hall. ER sent me to the eye surgeon and they operated Thursday morning, a detached retina. There's a gas bubble in the eye and I have to keep my head down most of the day. Can't fly. Just letting you know.

Watch your sugars with less activity, and call if you get fevers or anything else concerning. We have not received any records from the ER or the eye surgeon; I've requested them. Please book a visit when you're able to get out.

documents.title: Ophthalmology Consultation and Operative Summary
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OPHTHALMOLOGY - ED CONSULTATION 12/03/2025 AND OPERATIVE SUMMARY 12/04/2025
(Records received on request; the ED record itself was not included.)

Consult: 61-year-old woman, called from the ED for painless loss of vision in the right eye starting three hours earlier, after she struck her head on a door frame. No flashes or floaters beforehand. History of diabetes, RA on immunosuppression, AA amyloidosis.
Visual acuity: OD 20/250, OS 20/25. Intraocular pressure normal both eyes. No pain, injection or photophobia. Left eye normal.
Dilated fundus exam OD: macula-off rhegmatogenous retinal detachment with a single retinal tear. OS: attached, no breaks.
Plan: urgent repair.

Operation 12/04/2025: pars plana vitrectomy, right eye, with endolaser to the break and gas tamponade. Uncomplicated.
Post-op: face-down positioning as instructed; no air travel or high altitude until the gas resolves. Drops per sheet. Follow-up with retina at 1 day, 1 week, then as directed. NKDA.

documents.title: Retina Follow-up
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE RETINA - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Visit 02/10/2026. Two months after vitrectomy with gas for a macula-off rhegmatogenous detachment of the right eye. Gas resolved. Retina attached 360 degrees. Visual acuity OD 20/80, OS 20/25. IOP normal. Plan: return in 3 months; report any new flashes, floaters or shadow promptly.

events.reason: Abdominal pain and fever; complicated diverticulitis

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Sigmoid colon wall thickening with pericolic fat stranding and a few small foci of extraluminal gas confined to the pericolic fat adjacent to the sigmoid. No drainable abscess. No free intraperitoneal air. No free fluid. Background sigmoid diverticulosis. Post-hysterectomy pelvis. Kidneys without hydronephrosis.
reports.conclusion: Acute sigmoid diverticulitis with localized perforation. No abscess.

reports.text: Portable AP view. Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. Cardiac silhouette normal in size. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
reports.conclusion: Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates with normal heart size.

reports.text: Portable AP view compared with 06/06/2026. Marked interval clearing of the bilateral infiltrates. Normal heart size. No effusion.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE HOSPITAL - DISCHARGE SUMMARY, GENERAL SURGERY
Admitted 06/04/2026. Discharged 06/13/2026.

62-year-old woman on immunosuppression for rheumatoid arthritis (methotrexate, prednisone 5 mg, tocilizumab), with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, AA amyloidosis, treated cervical squamous cell carcinoma and Paget disease of the nipple, and a right retinal detachment repaired six months ago. Admitted with increasing abdominal pain and fever, T 38.3 on arrival.

CT: sigmoid diverticulitis with localized perforation (small extraluminal gas foci confined to the pericolic fat), no abscess.
Treatment: bowel rest, IV piperacillin-tazobactam. Methotrexate and tocilizumab held. Stress-dose hydrocortisone, later back to prednisone 5 mg. Glargine continued with correction insulin.

Over the first 48 hours she developed hematochezia with hemoglobin falling from 10.2 to 7.4 g/dL and received three units of packed red cells. Bleeding stopped without endoscopic or surgical intervention.

Several hours after the third unit (06/06 evening) she became acutely short of breath: RR 28, SpO2 84% on room air, HR 96, BP 118/72. She was in distress, using accessory muscles, with diffuse crackles at both bases and fields, no wheeze. Heart sounds normal; no JVD; no leg edema. Urine output unchanged. Portable chest film: bilateral infiltrates with a normal cardiac silhouette. NT-proBNP 180 pg/mL.
Diagnosis: transfusion-related acute lung injury. Transferred to ICU on high-flow nasal oxygen; not intubated. Improved over 72 hours; on room air from 06/10. Chest film 06/11 nearly clear. Blood bank notified and reaction reported to the supplier.

Hemoglobin 9.6 after transfusion, 9.3 at discharge.

Discharge diagnoses: complicated sigmoid diverticulitis with localized perforation; lower GI bleeding with acute blood loss anemia; transfusion-related acute lung injury.
Discharge medications: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily to complete 14 days of antibiotic therapy; resume home medications; HOLD tocilizumab until surgical follow-up.
Follow-up: general surgery clinic in 4 weeks; colonoscopy 6-8 weeks after recovery; PCP within 2 weeks.
Note for future care: any transfusion only after blood bank review given TRALI.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Patient Portal Message
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Patient: I was in the hospital June 4 to 13. Diverticulitis with a small hole in the bowel, then bleeding, then they gave me blood and my lungs filled up and I was in the ICU a few days. I'm home on antibiotics. They said see you in 2 weeks. I'm wiped out.

documents.title: Patient Portal Message
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Janet, I'm so sorry - that's a lot. Glad you're home. We don't have the hospital paperwork yet; I've asked for it. Please finish every antibiotic dose, go to the ER for fever, worsening belly pain, blood in the stool or any trouble breathing. Front desk will call to set up a visit.

documents.title: Scheduling Call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called to schedule hospital follow-up. Pt says her sister is driving her to the surgeon and eye appointments and she can't manage another trip this month; she'll call back when she has a ride. Offered video visit; she prefers in person.

documents.title: General Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
OUTSIDE GENERAL SURGERY - CLINIC FOLLOW-UP
Visit 07/14/2026. Follow-up after admission for perforated sigmoid diverticulitis complicated by lower GI bleeding and TRALI. Antibiotics completed. No abdominal pain, eating normally, no further bleeding. Breathing back to baseline. Abdomen soft, nontender.
Plan: colonoscopy with GI, booked for September 2026. Tocilizumab may be restarted per rheumatology. We will discuss elective sigmoid resection after the colonoscopy. NKDA.
